title: Subject and stress pronouns: je, tu, on… moi, toi
summary: Who does it: je, tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles; and the stressed moi, toi, lui, eux after c'est, after a preposition or alone.
focus: Choosing the subject pronoun and the stress pronoun
content:
## The subject pronouns

| pronoun | meaning | example |
|---|---|---|
| **je** / **j'** | I | **Je parle.** **J'habite ici.** |
| **tu** | you (one person, familiar) | **Tu parles anglais ?** |
| **il** | he, it | **Il est grand.** |
| **elle** | she, it | **Elle est ici.** |
| **on** | we (speech); one, people | **On mange ?** |
| **nous** | we | **Nous parlons.** |
| **vous** | you (polite, or several people) | **Vous parlez anglais ?** |
| **ils** | they (men or a mixed group) | **Ils sont là.** |
| **elles** | they (women only) | **Elles sont là.** |

**Je** becomes **j'** before a vowel or a silent h: **j'aime**, never *je aime*. **Il** and **elle** also stand for things: **la table → elle**, **le livre → il**.

## On, ils and elles

**On** is everywhere in spoken French. In conversation it means **we**, and the verb takes the **il / elle** form:

- **On mange au café ?** (Shall we eat at the café?) = **Nous mangeons au café ?**
- **On parle français à la maison.** (We speak French at home.)

For *they*, look at the group:

- **elles** only when everyone in it is female: **Léa et Inès → elles**.
- **ils** for men, and for any mixed group, even ten women and one man: **Marie et Paul → ils**.

## Tu or vous: with whom?

| **tu** | **vous** |
|---|---|
| a friend, a classmate | someone you don't know |
| your family | a shop assistant, a doctor |
| a child, a pet | your teacher, your boss |
| | **any** group of two or more |

The verb changes with the pronoun: **tu parles**, **vous parlez**. If you are unsure, start with **vous**; when someone says **On se tutoie ?**, you can switch to **tu**.

## Stress pronouns: moi, toi, lui, eux

| subject | **je** | **tu** | **il** | **elle** | **nous** | **vous** | **ils** | **elles** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stress | **moi** | **toi** | **lui** | **elle** | **nous** | **vous** | **eux** | **elles** |

Use a stress pronoun where no verb follows it:

- after **c'est**: **C'est moi.** (It's me.)
- after a preposition: **avec toi** (with you), **chez lui** (at his place), **pour elles** (for them)
- on its own: **Qui parle anglais ? — Moi !**
- for emphasis, before the subject: **Moi, je parle anglais. Lui, il parle espagnol.**
- in short replies: **Et toi ?** (And you?) **Moi aussi.** (Me too.)

vocabulary.meaning: I (j' before a vowel or a silent h)
vocabulary.example: J'habite à Lille et je parle anglais.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I live in Lille and I speak English.

vocabulary.example: Tu parles espagnol, Léa ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Do you speak Spanish, Léa?

vocabulary.meaning: you (polite, or more than one person)
vocabulary.example: Vous êtes madame Martin ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you Mrs Martin?

vocabulary.example: On mange ensemble ce soir ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Shall we eat together tonight?

vocabulary.example: Paul et Marie ? Ils habitent à Nice.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Paul and Marie? They live in Nice.

vocabulary.example: Léa et Inès ? Elles sont à l'école.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léa and Inès? They're at school.

vocabulary.example: Qui veut du café ? — Moi !
vocabulary.example_meaning: Who wants coffee? — Me!

vocabulary.example: Je viens avec toi.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm coming with you.

vocabulary.example: Ce soir, on dîne chez lui.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tonight we're having dinner at his place.

vocabulary.meaning: them (stressed; men or a mixed group)
vocabulary.example: Ce gâteau est pour eux.
vocabulary.example_meaning: This cake is for them.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'I live in Marseille'?
quiz.explanation: Je becomes j' before a vowel or a silent h, and habiter starts with a silent h: j'habite.
hints: Habiter starts with a silent h.

quiz.prompt: Paul et Marie ? ___ habitent à Nice. (They live in Nice.)
quiz.explanation: Paul and Marie are a mixed group, and a mixed group is always ils. Elles is only for groups that are all female.
hints: There is a man in the group.

quiz.prompt: Your new neighbour is an older woman you have just met. Which 'you' do you use with her?
quiz.explanation: Use vous with someone you don't know or someone older, until they suggest tu. Tu is for friends, family and children.
hints: Is she a friend or a stranger?

quiz.prompt: Léa, Inès et Chloé ? ___ sont au café. (They're at the café.)
quiz.explanation: Three women and no man: the pronoun is elles.
hints: Everyone in the group is female.

quiz.prompt: In 'On mange à midi ?', on means 'we' and mange is the il / elle form of the verb.
quiz.explanation: In everyday French, on replaces nous, but its verb always takes the il / elle form: on mange, not on mangeons.
hints: Compare il mange and on mange.

quiz.explanation: A pronoun standing on its own, with no verb after it, is a stress pronoun: Moi ! Je always needs a verb, and me is never used alone.

quiz.prompt: Je dîne chez ___ ce soir. (I'm having dinner at his place tonight.)
quiz.explanation: After a preposition like chez, use the stress pronoun: chez lui (at his place). Il can only stand before a verb.
hints: After chez, avec or pour, il becomes…

quiz.prompt: Ces fleurs sont pour ___. (These flowers are for them: Paul and Marie.)
quiz.explanation: After pour, use a stress pronoun. For a mixed group (Paul and Marie), the stress pronoun of ils is eux.

quiz.prompt: 'Moi, je parle anglais' is wrong, because moi and je cannot appear together.
quiz.explanation: Putting moi before je is normal and adds emphasis: Moi, je parle anglais (Me, I speak English). The same goes for toi, tu and lui, il.

listening.text: Je m'appelle Hugo, et toi ?
listening.meaning: My name is Hugo, and you?
listening.note: Et toi ? turns the question back to a friend.

listening.text: Vous parlez français, madame ?
listening.meaning: Do you speak French, madam?
listening.note: Vous is polite with someone you don't know.

listening.text: Nous habitons à Lyon.
listening.meaning: We live in Lyon.

listening.text: On regarde un film ce soir ?
listening.meaning: Shall we watch a film tonight?
listening.note: On = nous in everyday speech, with the il form of the verb.

listening.text: Marc et Sophie sont chez eux.
listening.meaning: Marc and Sophie are at home.

listening.text: Mon frère travaille avec moi au bureau.
listening.meaning: My brother works with me at the office.
listening.note: New word: le bureau = the office.

listening.text: Moi, je préfère le thé, et lui, il préfère le café.
listening.meaning: I prefer tea, and he prefers coffee.
listening.note: Moi and lui add emphasis to je and il.

listening.text: C'est pour toi, ce petit cadeau ?
listening.meaning: Is this little present for you?
listening.note: New word: le cadeau = the present.

concept.title: On = people in general
concept.markdown:
**On** can also mean *people*, *you* or *they* in general, with no one in particular:

- **En France, on mange tard.** (In France, people eat late.)
- **Ici, on parle français.** (French is spoken here.)

The verb still takes the **il** form.

guide.tip: Not sure whether to say tu or vous to an adult? Say vous. Nobody minds being treated politely; some people mind tu from a stranger.

conversations.title: At a party
conversations.scenario: At Karim's birthday party, Inès starts talking to Tom, whom she has never met.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Salut ! Tu es un ami de Karim ?
lines.meaning: Hi! Are you a friend of Karim's?
lines.note: tu between young people at a party

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui ! Moi, c'est Tom. Et toi ?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Inès. Tu es ici avec qui ?
lines.meaning: Inès. Who are you here with?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Avec eux, là-bas : Paul et Marie.
lines.meaning: With them, over there: Paul and Marie.
lines.note: eux after a preposition; a mixed group

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ah, ils sont sympas ! Ils habitent près de chez moi.
lines.meaning: Oh, they're nice! They live near me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Et toi, tu es avec qui ?
lines.meaning: And you, who are you with?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Avec Léa et Chloé. Elles sont dans la cuisine.
lines.meaning: With Léa and Chloé. They're in the kitchen.
lines.note: elles: everyone in the group is female

lines.speaker: b
lines.note: vous for more than one person

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, nous étudions la musique. On adore ça !
lines.meaning: Yes, we study music. We love it!
lines.note: on = nous, with the il form of the verb

bites.title: Who's who
bites.rule: je (j' before a vowel), tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles. Il and elle also stand for things: la table → elle.

bites.title: On means we
bites.rule: In everyday speech, on means we. Its verb takes the il / elle form: on parle, on mange.
bites.example_meaning: Shall we eat at the café?

bites.title: Ils for any mixed group
bites.rule: Elles only when everyone is female. One man in the group and it's ils. Vous for strangers and for any group.
bites.example: Marie et Paul ? Ils sont là.

bites.title: Moi, toi, lui, eux
bites.rule: Stress pronouns stand alone, after c'est, after avec, chez, pour, and before the subject for emphasis: Moi, je…
bites.example: C'est pour moi ? — Oui, pour toi !
bites.example_meaning: Is it for me? — Yes, for you!

sorts.title: Ils or elles?
sorts.why: Elles only for an all-female group; men or any mixed group take ils.

sorts.title: Tu or vous?
sorts.why: Tu for one person you know well (or a pet); vous for strangers, people you respect, and any group.

sorts.title: Subject or stress pronoun?
sorts.why: A subject pronoun comes before its verb; stress pronouns come after c'est and prepositions.

spots.why: Je becomes j' before a vowel or a silent h: j'habite.
After a preposition, use the stress pronoun: pour eux.

spots.sentence: Je dîne chez il ce soir.
spots.why: After chez, use the stress pronoun: chez lui.
A pronoun on its own is a stress pronoun: Moi !

spots.sentence: Marie et Paul ? Elles sont là.

realm.content:
## Les pronoms à Eldmark

Before the quest, the mage counts the party: **Moi, je porte les potions. Toi, tu as l'épée.** Borin? **Lui, il garde le butin.** Nym and Séla? **Elles sont avec nous.** The orcs? **Eux, ils restent à la taverne.** Then everyone shouts: **On part !**

vocabulary.example: J'ai une épée et un bouclier.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have a sword and a shield.

vocabulary.example: Tu es un elfe ou un nain ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you an elf or a dwarf?

vocabulary.example: On part au donjon ce soir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We're leaving for the dungeon tonight.

vocabulary.example: Les orcs ? Ils dorment dans la forêt.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The orcs? They're sleeping in the forest.

vocabulary.example: Nym et Séla ? Elles sont dans la guilde.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nym and Séla? They're in the guild.

vocabulary.example: Moi, je porte les potions.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Me, I carry the potions.

vocabulary.example: Borin garde l'or chez lui.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Borin keeps the gold at his place.

vocabulary.example: On part sans eux ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are we leaving without them?

vocabulary.example: La quête commence demain.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The quest starts tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Le butin est dans le donjon.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The loot is in the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: Notre équipe a quatre héros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our party has four heroes.

bites.title: Le groupe d'aventuriers
bites.rule: Subject pronouns before the verb; stress pronouns alone, for emphasis or after a preposition: Moi, je porte les potions. Le butin est pour eux.
bites.example: Toi, tu as l'épée ; lui, il a le bouclier.
bites.example_meaning: You have the sword; he has the shield.

listening.text: La quête commence avec nous.
listening.meaning: The quest starts with us.
listening.note: New word: la quête = the quest.

listening.text: Le butin, c'est pour eux ?
listening.meaning: The loot, is it for them?
listening.note: New word: le butin = the loot.

listening.text: Moi, je suis la mage du groupe.
listening.meaning: Me, I'm the group's mage.

listening.text: Borin et Séla ? Ils sont à la taverne.
listening.meaning: Borin and Séla? They're at the tavern.

listening.text: On part ce soir avec toi.
listening.meaning: We're leaving tonight with you.

spots.sentence: Borin et Séla ? Elles sont là.
spots.why: Borin is a man, so the mixed pair takes ils.
After avec, use the stress pronoun: avec toi.

sorts.title: Subject or stress pronoun in Eldmark?
sorts.why: A subject pronoun comes before its verb; a stress pronoun follows c'est or a preposition.

quiz.prompt: Borin the dwarf and the mage Séla walk into the taverne. Which pronoun stands for the pair of them?
quiz.explanation: One man in the group is enough: Borin and Séla are ils. Elles is only for an all-female group.

quiz.prompt: Le butin ? C'est pour ___ ! (The loot? It's for me!)
quiz.explanation: After pour (and after c'est), use the stress pronoun: pour moi.

meadowbrook.content:
## Les pronoms à Meadowbrook

At the harvest festival, Nora meets the town. To the mairesse: **Vous êtes la mairesse ?** To Léo, a friendly neighbour: **Tu pêches demain ?** Rosa and Léo? **Ils vendent des fraises.** The hens? **Elles sont avec moi.** And the whole town: **On fête les récoltes !**

vocabulary.example: Tu arroses les fraises, Léo ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you watering the strawberries, Léo?

vocabulary.example: Vous vendez du maïs, madame ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Do you sell corn, madam?

vocabulary.example: On récolte les citrouilles demain.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We're harvesting the pumpkins tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Rosa et Léo ? Ils sont à la plage.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa and Léo? They're at the beach.

vocabulary.example: Les poules ? Elles mangent du maïs.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hens? They're eating corn.

vocabulary.example: Ce champignon est pour toi.
vocabulary.example_meaning: This mushroom is for you.

vocabulary.example: Léo pêche, et moi, je pêche avec lui.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo is fishing, and I'm fishing with him.

vocabulary.example: La poule est dans le jardin.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hen is in the garden.

vocabulary.example: Ma voisine s'appelle Rosa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My neighbour is called Rosa.

vocabulary.example: La fête des récoltes est en automne.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The harvest festival is in autumn.

bites.title: Les voisins de Meadowbrook
bites.rule: Vous for the mairesse, tu for Léo. Ils for Rosa and Léo together, elles for the hens. On = all of us.
bites.example: Vous êtes la mairesse ? — Oui, et toi, tu es Nora ?
bites.example_meaning: Are you the mayor? — Yes, and you, are you Nora?

listening.text: Ma voisine arrose les fraises avec moi.
listening.meaning: My neighbour waters the strawberries with me.
listening.note: New word: la voisine = the neighbour.

listening.text: Les poules ? Elles sont à la ferme.
listening.meaning: The hens? They're at the farm.
listening.note: New word: la poule = the hen.

listening.text: On plante le maïs ensemble ?
listening.meaning: Shall we plant the corn together?

listening.text: Léo et Rosa sont chez eux.
listening.meaning: Léo and Rosa are at home.

listening.text: Toi, tu récoltes les citrouilles ?
listening.meaning: And you, are you harvesting the pumpkins?

spots.sentence: Rosa et Léo ? Elles sont au marché.
spots.why: Léo is a man, so the pair takes ils.

spots.sentence: Je plante le maïs avec il.
spots.why: After avec, use the stress pronoun: avec lui.

sorts.title: Tu or vous at Meadowbrook?

items.text: the mairesse, the first time you meet

sorts.why: Tu for one friend, a child or a pet; vous for someone new or important, and for any group.

quiz.prompt: Nora meets the mairesse for the first time. How does she ask her name?
quiz.explanation: A first meeting with the mayor calls for vous: Comment vous appelez-vous ? Tu is for friends and children.
hints: Is the mayor a close friend?

quiz.prompt: 'Les poules ? Ils sont à la ferme.' uses the right pronoun for the hens.
quiz.explanation: La poule is feminine and the hens are all female, so the pronoun is elles: Les poules ? Elles sont à la ferme.

rustwake.content:
## Les pronoms à Rustwake

Outside the Dôme, you meet the locals. To the foreman: **Vous êtes le contremaître Ruiz ?** To Léo: **Je viens avec toi !** Léo and Marta? **Ils échangent des écrous.** Marta and her goat? **Elles dorment à l'atelier.** The garden robot? **Lui, il répare tout.** And the scavengers: **On explore le désert.**

vocabulary.example: J'explore le désert de rouille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm exploring the rust desert.

vocabulary.example: Vous êtes le contremaître Ruiz ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you the foreman, Ruiz?

vocabulary.example: On échange des écrous contre de l'eau ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Shall we trade nuts for water?

vocabulary.example: Léo et Marta ? Ils sont au marché.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo and Marta? They're at the market.

vocabulary.example: Le robot jardinier ? Je travaille avec lui.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The garden robot? I work with it.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche de l'eau avec toi, Léo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm looking for water with you, Léo.

vocabulary.example: Les fouilleurs ? On part avec eux.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The scavengers? We're leaving with them.

vocabulary.example: Le robot jardinier arrose les tomates.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The garden robot waters the tomatoes.

vocabulary.example: Marta compte ses écrous.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta counts her nuts.

vocabulary.example: La marchande vend de l'eau filtrée.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The trader sells filtered water.

bites.title: Dehors, avec les autres
bites.rule: Vous for Ruiz the foreman, tu for Léo. Ils for Léo and Marta, elles for Marta and her goat. On = us scavengers.
bites.example: Vous êtes Ruiz ? Moi, je suis Léo.
bites.example_meaning: Are you Ruiz? Me, I'm Léo.

listening.text: Le robot jardinier travaille avec nous.
listening.meaning: The garden robot works with us.
listening.note: New word: le robot jardinier = the garden robot.

listening.text: On échange de l'eau contre des écrous.
listening.meaning: We trade water for nuts.

listening.text: Vous venez avec nous, monsieur Ruiz ?
listening.meaning: Are you coming with us, Mr Ruiz?

listening.text: Les fouilleurs ? Moi, je pars sans eux.
listening.meaning: The scavengers? Me, I'm leaving without them.

listening.text: La marchande parle avec lui.
listening.meaning: The trader is talking with him.
listening.note: New word: la marchande = the trader.

spots.why: After pour, use the stress pronoun: pour lui.

spots.sentence: Léo et Marta ? Elles cherchent de l'eau.
spots.why: Léo is a man, so the pair takes ils.

sorts.title: Ils or elles in the desert?
sorts.why: Elles only for an all-female group (la chèvre is feminine); any man or masculine noun in the group makes it ils.

quiz.prompt: On part avec ___ : Léo et Ruiz. (We're leaving with them.)
quiz.explanation: After avec, use a stress pronoun; for men or a mixed group it's eux.
hints: After a preposition, not the subject pronoun.

quiz.prompt: ___ échange des écrous contre de l'eau. (We trade nuts for water, in everyday speech.)
quiz.explanation: Échange is the il / elle form, so the everyday 'we' is on: On échange des écrous. Nous would need échangeons.
hints: The verb has the il form, but the meaning is 'we'.
